## The depreciation formula {#fm5-depreciation-formula .fm-slide }

::: {.takeaway}
$$S=\textcolor{#3b66a8}{V_0}\left(1-\frac{\textcolor{#b55224}{d}}{100}\right)^{\textcolor{#007f78}{n}}$$
:::

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $V_0$ | Initial value |
| $d$ | Percentage depreciation rate per period |
| $n$ | Number of periods |
| $S$ | Value remaining after those periods |

<p class="small-note">Repeated decrease uses a multiplier between 0 and 1.</p>

::: notes
Booklet §4.2, p. 13. Establish the formula by repeated multiplication by (1−d/100), using the same structure as compound growth. S is the remaining or salvage value, not the accumulated loss. For this model assume 0<d<100.
:::
